exposure: surgical vaginoscopy via no-touch hysteroscopic approach
outcome: surgical outcomes (duration, bleeding volume, hospitalization, complications)
pathological diagnoses (endometrial polyps, cervical polyps, vaginal polyps, vaginal stump polyps)
coincidence rate between intraoperative and pathological diagnosis
delivery outcomes (full term delivery, caesarean delivery, miscarriage, placental abruption)
cohort: Forty-six patients (average age 33.0 ± 8.8 years) diagnosed with genital polyps, including 25 non-pregnant and 21 pregnant women, who underwent operative vaginoscopy.
finding: Surgical vaginoscopy via a no-touch hysteroscope is a minimally invasive, highly effective, and safe method for addressing female reproductive tract polyps, demonstrating significant clinical value, particularly for cervical polyps during pregnancy.
mod_finding: Nineteen pregnant patients delivered at full term, while one underwent caesarean delivery at 31 weeks due to placental abruption, and one experienced a miscarriage at 18 weeks of gestation.
followup_time: 2 months post-surgery for non-pregnant patients; until delivery for pregnant patients.
gest_age: Full term for 19 deliveries; 31 weeks for one caesarean delivery; 18 weeks for one miscarriage.
